contexts.text: The third (river of Eden) = reason.

The river Hiddekel = reason, or the clear perspicacity of reason... The river goeth eastward towards Asshur = that the perspicacity of reason comes from the Lord through the internal man into the rational mind, which is of the external man.
From Him is wisdom; through wisdom intelligence; through intelligence reason; thus through reason are vivified the scientifics which are of the memory. Signified.
He says, Have not animals something analogous to reason?
So that reason no longer remained; but ratiocination. Treated of.
The lowest things of reason; that is, scientifics. Signified.
As the wife does not act from reason so much as the man...
The happiness increases in the ratio of the numbers.
The male sex is so formed that understanding or reason reigns...
By reason, and rational things, are properly meant things which are true; and by ratiocination, and reasoning, things which are false. Illustrated.
The Knowledges of truth are from the Lord through... faith, by the medium of reason and knowledge.
In such a ratio is the speech of Spirits...
New-born infants are not endowed with reason.
There are many now who believe nothing, unless they know from reason that it is so... Therefore these things [are explained].

The celestial regard these things from good; but the spiritual from truth; and are also confirmed, and thus perfected, by such things as are in the internal sense; but this by thousands of interior reasons which cannot inflow perceptibly into man's idea.
An account will have to be rendered of the thoughts, etc.
When nothing is acknowledged... except what can be apprehended by reason.
No ratio between the infinite and the finite. AC 4383:end. DP 54.

When the doctrine of faith is regarded from Divine truths... all the rational and scientific things confirm it; but when from... reason and knowledge, nothing of good or of truth is conceived. For to regard from the Word, is to do so from the Lord; but to regard from reason and knowledge, is to do so from man; (and) from these are all insanity and folly.

Man cannot be regenerated till adult age, because he then first is strong in reason and judgment, and thus can receive good and truth from the Lord. Before he comes into this state, he is being prepared. Explained.
Celestial men do not even confirm by reasons... but only say that it is so, or is not so.

The first (general operation of Heaven) is into the brain at the left temple, and is a general operation as to the organs of reason; for the left part of the brain corresponds to rational or intellectual things...
An eagle, here, = reason, which is of intelligence.
They might have known from themselves much about these things if they had wanted to use their reason.
Light inflows from Heaven... and causes the reasons which he sees in his understanding to be so many rays of that light.
A person is led to his opinion... by both reasons and affections...
(Such can see) that animals act from instinct, and man from reason...
Beasts follow their affections from instinct, without reason... To these affections without reason no other bodily forms are suitable...
(These Spirits) cannot attend to reasons, because they persist tenaciously in their own opinion. AC 5554:end.
May be evident to him who concludes from reason.

When he becomes a youth, if he cultivates his Rational, he thus, from the things in the interior Natural, forms reasons, which are truths still more sublime, and as it were extracted from those in the interior Natural. The ideas of thought from these are called... intellectual and immaterial ideas...
Man cannot live from general influx, like animals devoid of reason.
For man is born without any use of reason, and can be initiated into it only through influx from the Heavens.

First of all there is insinuated with man general truth: this is then enriched with particular truths, and lastly there comes forth from the Internal a mental view of these, or reason and understanding.

(As soon as good dominates) the affection itself and the derivative reason dominate, and subjugate in the Natural the delights of the love of self and of the world, and also the fallacies which had infilled the scientifics there...
So that the proportion (in the Grand Man) may be maintained.
The things of the natural mind are called scientifics; and those of the rational mind, intellectual reasons... The latter are in the light of Heaven.
Nothing enters into the internal man except through intellectual ideas, which are reasons; for the ground which receives there is the illustrated Rational.
Leviathan, in a good sense, = reason from truths. Reason from truths is opposite to reasonings from falsities.
Thus (are good Spirits caused) to consider whether the case is so, and to collect reasons, and thus to bring that truth into their minds rationally...
After regeneration, he enjoys this delight... in an opposite manner.
A just proportion to everyone, in particular, and in general. Signified, Explained.
There is no ratio between the temporary and the eternal...

For when man is in these (bodily pleasures) he but little consults his reason, and thus is but little conscious... When a beast is called a beast of burden, it = the merely corporeal affections which in themselves have little of reason; for the more a man acts from the body, the less he acts from reason; for the body is in the world, and thus remote from Heaven, where genuine reason is.
Hence the celestial Angels... being in the highest light, do not even confirm truths by reasons...
External men confirm Divine truths by oaths; but internal men by reasons...
The relation (or mode) of the influx from what is higher. Signified, Explained.
See Reason, To.
In a like manner...
A man may perceive (this) from reason alone...
For it is from order that everyone should act from reason...
Hence it is that man... can speak from reason.
Still, there can never be any proportion between the wisdom of the Angels and that of the Lord... for no proportion is possible between the infinite and the finite. SE 5566.
Those who think from interior reason can see that...
Everyone who thinks from any illustrated reason can see that...
In that a man acts from reason, and a woman from affection.
Acting in freedom according to reason.

It is from Divine order that man should act from freedom according to reason; because to act from freedom according to reason is to act from himself. But these two faculties, freedom and reason, are not proper to man; but are the Lord's with him; and... without them he cannot be reformed...
(In order that He may be loved reciprocally) the Lord has given to man freedom and reason...
Therefore man must render an account of his works.

All things of human reason... concentrate in this: that there is one God, the Creator of the universe; and therefore a man who has reason, thinks, from the general of his understanding, no otherwise... Say to anyone who has sound reason, that there are two Creators of the universe, and you will be sensible of his repugnance... The very faculty of thinking rationally, regarded in itself, is not of man, but is of God with him; from this faculty depends human reason in general, and this general causes him to see this as if of himself.
But if a man by this faculty has perverted the lower parts of his understanding... by the twisting of them, he turns this faculty in another direction; and hence his reason becomes unsound.
Reception is according to the application of the laws of order... from the freedom of thinking and willing according to reason, which they have from the Lord as their own.
For the rule of the one is the same as that of the other.
This is testified by reason and experience. Explained.
(Thus) wisdom can be elevated in a triplicate ratio; and in each degree it may be perfected to its height in a simple ratio.
Thus there is a ratio between the finite and the infinite; not from the finite, but from the infinite in the finite.
That it is a law of the Divine Providence that man should act from freedom according to reason. Chapter.
Under Rational, see this reference.
That whatever man does from freedom, whether it be of reason, or not of reason, provided it is according to his reason, appears to him as his. General article.
When evil has been confirmed, it appears as of reason.
Under Free, see this reference. DP 97. DP 98. DP 183:2.
Everyone can see from reason alone that...

There are many things which when heard are at once perceived to be so... but if they are not at the same time confirmed by reasons, they may be weakened by arguments from fallacies, and at last be denied.

For that which the Lord teaches, He gives to man to perceive by reason; and this in two ways: one, that he sees in himself that it is so as soon as he hears it; the other, that he understands it by means of reasons. To see in himself, is to see in the internal man; and to understand by means of reasons, is in the external man.

Foreknowledge of events is not given to man, in order that he may be able to act from freedom according to reason; for... whatever a man loves he wants to effect, and he leads himself to it by reason; moreover, there is nothing which a man considers with reason, which is not from the love that it may come into effect through the thought; and therefore if he knew the effect... his reason would become quiescent; and, with his reason, his love; for the love ceases with reason in the effect; and from that it then begins anew. It is the delight itself of reason, that from the love it sees the effect in the thought; not in the effect, but before it... Hence man has what is called hope, which increases and decreases in the reason, as he sees or anticipates the event...
One who... believes that human prudence does all things, cannot be convinced except by reasons of a deeper investigation. Enumerated.

(Thus) man can abuse these faculties, and from freedom according to reason confirm anything he likes; for he can make to be of reason anything he wants, whether it be in itself of reason, or not. Example(s).
I said, Do you want me to speak to you... from reason, or from Holy Scripture. They said, Speak first from reason...
(This) may be confirmed before reason; thus...
Who cannot see from reason, if he wants to see, that...
(This) must be so delivered by me that reason also may assent thereto.

Wisdom, regarded in its fullness, is at the same time of Knowledges, of reason, and of life. Knowledges precede; reason is formed through them; and wisdom through both, when a man lives rationally according to the Truths which are Knowledges. (Continued. See Wisdom.)
They then say, We hold reason under obedience to faith.
That adulteries of the third degree are adulteries of reason...
What has been torn may be made whole, when the reason of man is convinced, from the Word and the derivative lumen, that...
All sound reason, although not religious, sees that...
That human reason, from many things in the world, is able to perceive, if it wants, that there is a God, and that He is one. Explained.
That illustrated reason, from very many things in the world, can see the infinity of God. Explained.
Human reason can see this from... TCR 41.

(This) reason, left to itself, can by no means see... There is nothing else than for man to approach the Lord God the Saviour, and read the Word under His auspices... and he will be illustrated, and will see Truths, which reason also will acknowledge.

In this mystical notion... reason has no part; (and) when reason is lulled, the speech of the mouth is a something inanimate. When the mouth utters that from which reason dissents, the speech is fatuous. At this day, human reason is bound, in relation to the Divine Trinity...

(Such) have no interior reason of judgment... but only ingenuity, from which they can... confirm whatever presents itself as if from reason; but the objects of reason which they principally love are falsities...
The angelic Spirit said to them... Bring together the reasons which I shall offer, and make a conclusion from them yourselves...
The states of faith of the New Church are... 3. Faith of memory; faith of reason; faith of light.
Blind faith is that of mystical Things, which are believed, although it is not known... whether they are above reason, or contrary to it.

Unless there were such an ordination of substances in the mind, man would not have anything analytic of reason, which everyone has according to the ordination; thus according to the abundance of Truths which cohere as in a bundle; and the ordination is according to the use of reason from freedom.
This manifests itself before everyone who collects reasons.
(This) Scripture teaches, and reason also sees.
In the understanding (the will) puts itself in light, that it may see not only the reasons, but also the occasions...

(Thus) man is man in proportion as he speaks from sound reason, and regards his abode in Heaven; and he is not man, in proportion as he speaks from perverted reason, and regards only his stay in the world...
For the good of the will forms itself in the understanding, and there presents itself to view in the light of reason.
From reason itself, man can see that...
Who does not see, if he can think from reason elevated above the sensuous things of the body, that...
The reason man does not know this from any light of reason, is that fallacies... cast a shade on this light.
They replied, In our universal theology there is not anything spiritual which reason apprehends...
(This) anyone can conclude from reason.
Everyone will acknowledge this to be so, provided he adjoins reason to experience.
Who cannot understand, from the reason given him, that...
(This) is evident from all reason.
Unless the understanding could be perfected separately... man... would not be able to act from reason; but from instinct.
Into faith they suffer no reason to be admitted...
Ask anyone who is endowed with religion, and at the same time with reason...
Reason itself assents to this: that...
In what way the Lord is present...
(This) reason itself dictates.
When they mention faith and omnipotence, reason is exiled; and then sound reason either disappears... or becomes like a spectre, and is called insanity.
The interior operations of the natural mind, when perverted, are called ratiocinations; but, when according to order, they are simply called reason...
(The Spirits of Saturn) relate to that in man which is called the internal sense, or reason.
The reason is that which as it were ascends into the intellectual mind... for the more interior mind understands through the internal sense, or reason.
Thus we ought to believe the Truths spoken by the Lord... although we do not penetrate them by reason...
The Spirits of our Earth relate to the external sense, and at this day are almost separated from all reason; and those of Saturn relate to reason. Thus was manifested their quality against reason.

When the Spirits of our Earth perceive the sphere of reason, and of the Spirits who relate to reason, they cannot endure them: there is a natural enmity... a like enmity have all men here against reason; but they do not perceive it, except in temptations; because the reason as it were yields from afar, and there succeeds what is irrational with its phantasies.
The nature of the conflict of reason with the external senses separated...

For it is according to the order in the world that everyone uses his reason, and that things follow according to reason; but, as they do not believe that God inspires reason... they reject the Divine regimen...
The English have a sufficiently exquisite perception when anything is said from reason...
In the Spiritual World it is forbidden to speak from what is persuasive; but [they must speak] from reason, and thus from truths themselves.
(Such philosophical things) take away all reason.
For sensuous men who are in falsities of evil... do not fight from reason against truths... (but) solely from a persuasion of falsity.
Take away the use of reason, and say that some man of authority has seen it, and (you may persuade some that a crow is white).
By which he procures for himself the lumen of reason.
He who believes that any truth of the Church can be seen from the lumen of reason alone, is much mistaken...
The reason is that...
There is no ratio between the Natural, the Spiritual, and the Celestial. DWis 12. 4.
2. (Confirmations) from reason given. DWis 2. 3. DWis 7. 2. 4. DWis 7. 3. 2. DeDomino 20. DeDomino 55.
It is allowable to confirm the Truths of the Church by reason...
